explanation: Gift-giving isn't a standard part of UK business culture, and an expensive or elaborate gift can come across as inappropriate or even like an attempted bribe; a modest gesture like good chocolates or a bottle of wine is more common than a formal gift exchange. If you're invited to someone's home, bringing wine, flowers, or chocolates for the host is a thoughtful touch - many people avoid all-white or lily arrangements due to their strong association with funerals, and very romantic gestures like red roses, when the occasion is simply a dinner invitation.
local_tip: If invited to a colleague's home, bring a bottle of wine, a box of chocolates, or a seasonal bouquet - skip lilies and keep any gift modest rather than lavish.

also_check.note: Gift-giving is a highly ritualized and expected part of business culture; careful presentation and wrapping matter a great deal.
Gifts can seem unnecessary or even slightly suspicious in formal business settings until a relationship is well established.
Gift-giving is common and appreciated, but should respect Islamic customs - avoid alcohol and pork, and give with the right hand.
